notes: Hall not identified: the A4 experimental halls at MAMI are not located in any fetched source; placed at the institute's campus-grade site (site:mainz-kph-campus).

Dates are partial and uncertain: January and September 2003 beam times are dated in a 2004 conference talk, the end is only bounded (before September 2018), and the start of the programme (1996, collaboration investigating strangeness) is dated by a 2007 thesis.
Three results are recorded (2004, 2009, 2020); other A4 papers (Q^2 = 0.108 forward result, transverse-asymmetry papers of 2005 and 2017, deuterium result of 2016) are not.
Official pages: the collaboration page and publication list are hosted by AG Maas, Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz; the page lists current and former members but states no start, end or status.

physics_goals.quote: The difference is a direct measurement of the strangeness contribution to the vector form factors of the proton.
physics_goals.value: Measure the strange-quark contribution to the vector form factors of the proton through the parity-violating asymmetry in polarised electron-proton scattering

summary.plain: A4 scattered spin-polarised electrons from hydrogen and deuterium at the Mainz microtron MAMI and counted them with a lead-fluoride calorimeter. The tiny difference between the two spin directions shows how much strange quarks contribute to the proton's electric and magnetic structure, which proved to be small.
summary.technical: Counting-mode parity-violating electron scattering at MAMI: longitudinally polarised electrons (about 80% polarisation, 20 uA) on a 10 cm liquid-hydrogen (and deuterium) target, scattered electrons recorded in a 1022-crystal PbF2 Cherenkov calorimeter in forward (30-40 degree) or backward (140-150 degree) configuration, to separate the strange electric and magnetic form factors G_E^s and G_M^s; results at Q^2 = 0.230 (A_phys = -5.44 +- 0.54 +- 0.27 ppm) and 0.22 (GeV/c)^2, plus beam-transverse-spin asymmetries up to 1.5 GeV.
